candidates.title: The Door Was Never Fully Closed
candidates.one_line_concept: After a small fight, one of them goes to the other room but leaves the door slightly open, because the argument needs distance but love does not.
candidates.emotional_truth: Real couples often perform being angry while secretly keeping a path back open.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Send this to the person who knows your dramatic exit still comes with a soft re-entry policy.
candidates.visual_evidence: Aachu on one side of a half-open bedroom door, Zuv visible in the other room through a thin strip of warm light; neither is looking at the other, but the door is visibly unlatched.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium-low. It must stay petty, domestic, and specific: not heartbreak, just a tiny fight with an open door.

candidates.title: The Packet Pause
candidates.one_line_concept: One of them is on an important call, and the other freezes mid-snack-opening like the packet has become a bomb.
candidates.emotional_truth: Love is often not grand support; it is ridiculous self-control for exactly seventeen seconds.
candidates.relatable_trigger: For couples who know the sound of chips can become a relationship test.
candidates.visual_evidence: Zuv on a laptop call, Aachu beside him holding a half-torn snack packet in both hands, face fully guilty, body frozen; crumbs and tea nearby.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Low. It is not supporting your dreams; it is the tiny choreography of not ruining someone's call with packet thunder.

candidates.title: The Correct Bite Treaty
candidates.one_line_concept: They both pretend to eat normally, but each keeps saving the best corner of the snack for the other.
candidates.emotional_truth: Intimacy is knowing which bite is the good bite and giving it away without announcing the sacrifice.
candidates.relatable_trigger: For couples with very serious unspoken food negotiations.
candidates.visual_evidence: One plate between them, a sandwich or dosa torn unevenly, the crispest saucy corner untouched and nudged toward the other person with no speech.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium. Food-sharing can get cute-card fast; the idea only works if the visual is about the exact best bite, not vague sharing.

candidates.title: The Alarm That Is Not For Me
candidates.one_line_concept: One phone has an alarm named after the other person's thing: appointment, train, medicine, deadline, tiny chaos.
candidates.emotional_truth: Being loved sometimes means your life has quietly become someone else's reminder list.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Send this to the person whose calendar has suspiciously become a shared survival system.
candidates.visual_evidence: Two phones on the bed; one alarm label reads something practical and intimate like 'Aachu leave by 7:40' while the owner of that phone is not Aachu.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium. It risks generic care unless the alarm label is funny, practical, and visibly specific.

candidates.title: The Room-To-Room Translation Service
candidates.one_line_concept: One starts talking from another room at impossible volume, and the other walks closer instead of saying 'what?' for the fifth time.
candidates.emotional_truth: Couple patience is not always noble; sometimes it is learning the exact acoustics of someone you love.
candidates.relatable_trigger: For the person who begins conversations from the kitchen like the house has subtitles.
candidates.visual_evidence: Aachu half-visible in another room talking while doing something else; Zuv has abandoned the sofa and is standing in the hallway, listening with resigned affection.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Low-medium. It must avoid making one partner foolish; the affection is in the practiced accommodation, not the complaint.

candidates.title: The Subtitles Came On Without Discussion
candidates.one_line_concept: One person is eating something too crunchy during a movie, so the other silently turns subtitles on instead of starting a fight.
candidates.emotional_truth: Soft partnership is choosing the workaround before the complaint.
candidates.relatable_trigger: For couples whose movie nights include snacks loud enough to need accessibility settings.
candidates.visual_evidence: A movie playing with subtitles, one remote in hand, one person crunching happily, the other looking sideways but choosing peace.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Low. It is funny, stageable, and behavior-led; the only risk is making it too sitcom instead of tender.

top_pick.title: The Door Was Never Fully Closed
top_pick.why: It has the strongest emotional voltage without becoming a quote card. The whole idea is visible in one object: a half-open door.

rejected_patterns: generic care where one partner is saintly
quote-card sentiment with no photographable behavior
risk_notes: Keep every idea anchored to a visible object or gesture.
Do not let care beats become one-sided.
The top pick needs tonal control: it should feel like a small domestic sulk, not a breakup scene.
Food and alarm concepts need exact labels, bites, and body language.
